fatal_errors: The proposed composition-to-property surrogate is fundamentally different from the target use of an MTP as a liquid-phase interatomic potential combined with free-energy perturbation.
It replaces the wrong baseline: the relevant comparison is against EAM-based TOR-TILD thermodynamic integration, not primarily DSC, DTA, or CALPHAD.
The claimed ±5–10% accuracy and applicability across the entire HEA composition space are not supported by the cited evidence.
It omits the decisive physical contributions from electronic excitations and solid-state short-range order.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested thermodynamic quantities and offers a reasonably clear held-out experimental falsification test, so it is a plausible alternative research program. It does not reconstruct the target method, however. The target relies on a phase-space-faithful MTP with sub-meV/atom training errors to make DFT free-energy perturbation rapidly convergent, under specified functionals, pressure, temperature, and cell-size conditions. The generated mechanism is instead generic descriptor-based regression and contains none of the FEP-versus-TI rationale, electronic Gibbs-energy correction, DOS feature, or approximately 2.4 meV/atom SRO stabilization. Its quantitative outcomes also fail to match the target benchmarks of less than 0.5 meV/atom free-energy disagreement, roughly 80% savings or 20-fold speedup, and 48–57 K electronic shifts. The cited papers support CALPHAD, high-throughput calculations, and generic database limitations, but they do not establish the proposed hybrid model or its stated accuracy for fusion and liquid properties. The falsification design is useful for the alternative hypothesis, although allowing up to 30% of alloys to exceed 10% error is weak for a claim of family-wide accuracy.
